lines.text: Rain at Interlagos, a title for Mercedes, and a brand new Formula E car on track today.
lines.note: Rain returned, Mercedes title, Gen4 testing starts 16 Nov all supported.

lines.text: Lando Norris masters the rain in Brazil.
Mercedes are constructors' champions.
Formula E's GEN4 era begins at Jarama.
And a home debut nobody saw coming.
Lando Norris won from pole, by fourteen point six seconds.
lines.note: Pole (Silverstone), +14.602 (The Race).

lines.text: And the weather just would not make up its mind, all seventy-one laps of it.
lines.note: 71 laps (PlanetF1); changing weather (The Race).

lines.text: Kimi Antonelli actually jumped him at the start, and led until the first stops.
lines.note: Silverstone: Antonelli got ahead at Turn 1 and led, but retook-lead-by-Norris came after Antonelli spun on lap 20; PlanetF1 same. No source says he led 'until the first stops'. Say 'and led for a good part of the race' or 'until a spin on lap 20'.

lines.text: Charles Leclerc picked up a five-second penalty for forcing Liam Lawson wide, which handed seventh to Lawson.
No crashes, no safety car, in the wet, in Brazil.
lines.note: GPFans: no one crashed out, safety car never deployed.

lines.text: Honestly? Somebody check the calendar.
Max Verstappen started twenty-first, after grid penalties, and finished second.
lines.note: 21st confirmed; grid muddled by wet quali and penalties.

lines.text: In twenty twenty-four he won this race from seventeenth on the grid, in the rain.
lines.note: Matches anecdotes.json; 17th, wet confirmed. 'Not his first Interlagos rescue' is fair.

lines.text: Team-mate Isack Hadjar came home third, so that's a double podium for Red Bull.
George Russell finished fourth and Kimi Antonelli fifth.
And that made Mercedes the twenty twenty-six constructors' champions.
lines.note: Silverstone confirms.

lines.text: Interlagos again, Pix! They clinched the constructors' title here in twenty eighteen too, the day Hamilton won.
lines.note: Confirmed on page.

lines.text: From today until Friday, the whole grid is testing at Jarama.
lines.note: 16-20 Nov confirmed.

lines.text: It's the GEN4 car's first collective test, and the series calls it its most advanced and powerful car yet.
Season thirteen is the biggest so far: twenty-one races at thirteen events in eleven countries.
lines.note: 'Biggest' is not in any source I read; CGTN says 'longest in Formula E history' with 21 rounds. Thirteen events / eleven countries could not be verified (Band page blocked, FIA/CGTN have no count). Use 'the longest season yet, with twenty-one races' unless the Band source confirms 13/11.

lines.text: It opens with a night double-header in Jeddah on the eighteenth and nineteenth of December, and Opel joins as a new manufacturer.
lines.note: Dates and Opel confirmed. 'Night' not verified. Time-sensitive: CGTN notes 'heavy doubt' over the Jeddah opener due to regional conflict; re-check before publishing.

lines.text: On the grid, Nissan pairs Oliver Rowland with Zane Maloney, and Jake Hughes returns at Cupra Kiro in place of Dan Ticktum.
lines.note: Nissan release also confirms.

lines.text: Pascal Wehrlein starts the new era as champion.
lines.note: No source in the notes or fetched pages names Wehrlein as Season 12 champion (Nissan says only Rowland was Season 11 champion). Cut or add a source.

lines.text: Byte, you wanted this one.
Did I ever! Rafael Camara, twenty-one, made his Grand Prix debut for Haas, at home in São Paulo.
He's signed for twenty twenty-seven, but Haas had confirmed Esteban Ocon would not return, so in he went.
With Gabriel Bortoleto in the Audi, Brazil had two home drivers in an F1 race for the first time since twenty sixteen.
Twenty sixteen! Felipe Massa retired after an accident that day, and Felipe Nasr came from twenty-first on the grid to finish ninth.
lines.note: Re-checked table: Nasr grid 21, 9th; Massa Ret, Accident.

lines.text: Alan Jones died on the fifth of November, aged eighty, after a short illness.
He won twelve Grands Prix between nineteen seventy-five and nineteen eighty-six.
Five of them came in nineteen eighty, and brought him the title in the Williams FW07B, the team's first.
lines.note: Five 1980 wins and Williams' first champion confirmed (Crash, Autosport, PlanetF1). The FW07B car is not named as the title car in any fetched source (Autosport only shows a photo). Cut 'FW07B' or add a source.

lines.text: He remains the last Australian to win the championship.
Arvid Lindblad finished just outside the points in eleventh for Racing Bulls.
Formula E will race twice in Shanghai, and Sanya moves to April twenty twenty-seven.
In IndyCar, Christian Lundgaard has signed a multi-year deal with Chip Ganassi Racing, taking Scott Dixon's seat, and Dennis Hauger is Rookie of the Year.
lines.note: Frontstretch returned 403; no other source checked. Could not verify.

lines.text: And Jack Harvey has announced a cancer diagnosis. He still intends to race in the twenty twenty-seven Indianapolis five hundred, and we wish him well.
lines.note: Sensitive health claim; source unreachable (403). Do not air unverified. Tone otherwise fine.

lines.text: Next up, the lights go out on the Las Vegas Strip, from the nineteenth to the twenty-first of November.
lines.note: Round 21, 19-21 Nov.

lines.text: Then it's Qatar on the twenty-ninth.
lines.note: Weekend 27-29 Nov; race Sunday 29th.

graphics.note: Jeddah 18-19 Dec: re-check for regional-conflict doubt.
HAUGER: ROOKIE OF YEAR unverified (Frontstretch 403). Cut with the line.
Las Vegas 19-21 Nov, Qatar 29 Nov, Jeddah 18-19 Dec.
